newsitem.title: USA: NYC Council wants to create superstore zoning plan.
newsitem.headline: NYC Council wants to create superstore zoning plan.

text.p: New York City Council leaders announced Wednesday they will create a zoning plan to allow superstores to be built more easily in industrial areas recommended by local community boards.
The annoucement by Council Speaker Peter Vallone came five months after the Council rejected Mayor Rudolph Giuliani's proposed zoning change to allow superstores "as of right" in manufacturing zones.

The key change Vallone proposed is to designate specific retail districts in manufacturing zones based on community board recommendations. The mayor's plan had prompted widespread community opposition.

Vallone proposed creating two types of retail districts: 55,000 square feet, seen as large enough for big supermarkets, and 125,000 square feet. Giuliani's proposal would have allowed developments of up to 200,000 square feet.
Vallone said he hoped to designate 60 sites that would already be approved by local communities, averting the controversey that surrounds major developments.
City Planning Commission Chairman Joseph Rose, Giuliani's spokesman on the issue, said Vallone had announced "a plan to have a plan," and said he looked forward to seeing the proposal when completed.
But Rose, who had criticized the Council sharply when it rejected the mayor's plan last December, said that if the Council can identify 60 sites for large stores, "that would be a constructive step."
